prompt: For each channel, what is the median of its campaigns' daily clicks from 1 July to 31 October 2025, both days included? spend_date is a UTC day, and each row of ad_spend_daily in that period is one value. The median is the middle value once the values are sorted; with an even number of values, it is the average of the two middle values. Return two columns, in this order: channel_id and median_clicks. Return one row for each channel with rows in that period. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per channel with rows in the period

hints: Next, write the median of the daily clicks as an aggregate, one value for each channel.
A continuous percentile at 0.5 is the median: it averages the two middle values when the count is even, which no plain average does.
why_this_works: percentile_cont(0.5) sorts each channel's daily clicks and takes the middle value, the average of the two middle ones when the count is even.
